stemMd: A city will reduce traffic by charging vehicles entering its center. It predicts fewer vehicle trips overall because entries to the center will fall. Which assumption connects the prediction to the evidence?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The reduction in center entries will not be offset by additional vehicle trips elsewhere.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Every vehicle entering the center carries only one person.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The charge will be identical to a neighboring city's charge.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The city center has no shops.

explanationMd: The evidence concerns one location while the conclusion concerns the whole system. Diversion or extra peripheral trips could offset the center's reduction. The missing assumption prevents that offset.

distractorRationale.b: Occupancy is not necessary to compare trip counts.
distractorRationale.c: A neighboring price does not determine net trips.
distractorRationale.d: Bicycle ownership is compatible with reduced car trips.
distractorRationale.e: Commercial activity does not establish the required net effect.
